newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's CEO 1996 pay at more than $2mln.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's CEO 1996 pay at more than $2mln.

text.p: Michael Quinlan, McDonald's Corp's chairman and chief executive officer, was paid more than $2 million in salary and bonus for 1996, an amount slightly lower than the previous year's compensation, the company said in a regulatory filing.

Overall, Quinlan received a salary of $1.116 million, was awarded a bonus of $932,000 and received $384,703 in other compensation, according to the Oakbrook, Ill. fast food chain's proxy filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
The company noted that based on his outstanding performance in 1995, his salary was increased on April 1, 1996 to $1,132,500 from $1,068,400.
In 1995, he received a salary of $1.05 million, but was awarded a bigger bonus of $1.05 million in addition to receiving other compensation of $362,937, according to the filing.

In 1996, Quinlan received options to purchase 331,000 shares of common stock. Of that amount, 300,000 can be exercised at a price of $49.25 each, with an expiration of April 1, 2006. The remaining 31,000 shares can be exercised at $52.125 each, with an expiration of March 18, 2006.
In 1995, Quinlan received options to purchase 529,000 shares.
Consistent with all other officers, Quinlan will not receive a merit increase in 1997, the company said in the filing.
